Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’m starting with the workspace contract and rollout evidence. I’ll use the `read-wake-visual-signals-first` skill to inspect both required views before touching the policy, then the explicitly requested `fish-control-primitives` skill to decide whether a mechanism transfers into this candidate.

The evidence bank is already late-lineage rather than a naive first proposal: it records repeated threshold captures plus substantial run-to-run terminal variability. I’m now comparing all four sampled rollouts—including the strongest finite capture and the most informative weaker capture—and checking whether any existing terminal modification has actually survived repetition before proposing one new mechanism.

The sampled set contains no visual failure—all four terminate in capture—so the required failure comparison comes from the assigned parent’s exact burden-allocation repeat (`1.8544L`, lower-domain exit). That distinction matters: the sampled captures support the carrier and intercept geometry, while the parent failure rejects promoting actuator-state steering allocation from its earlier one-off success. I’m inspecting those two combined sheets first, then the remaining sampled variants for wake consistency.

The visual/trace cross-check points to a cleaner mechanism than another gain or actuator reallocation. At the first `4L` crossing, every sampled capture has `|course error| ≤ 0.113 rad`, while the parent failure is already at `0.369 rad`; at `3L`, captures are `0.128–0.275 rad` and the failure is `0.489 rad`. The wake and speed remain healthy in both cases, so the separable defect is premature response-based steering release under persistent route error. The candidate will preserve the proven carrier and full steering allocation, adding only an error-aware veto to that release logic.

The shelf consultation now directly informs the edit: I’m translating its closed-loop “redirect, then release only after observed error has actually reduced” invariant. The skill steers this away from published gains or a new carrier tune; the proposed gate uses only normalized body-frame achieved-course error and leaves the posterior traveling bend untouched. I’m recording that transfer and its falsification boundary before editing the policy, as required.

The candidate and durable guidance are now updated. The guidance change closes the inherited open question: the burden-conditioned allocator’s exact repeat failed (`1/2` overall), so future workers should stop treating actuator-state allocation as the pending confirmation target. I’m moving to deterministic contract checks and a replay locality audit; no CFD will be run.

The policy’s Julia probe hit an environment issue: `julia` is not on this shell’s `PATH`, so this is not yet a candidate failure. I’m locating the workspace’s configured Julia binary while the required check-runner continues its independent checks.

All three mandated checks now pass; the Julia check succeeded with the installed 1.12.6 runtime. The replay audit also shows the intended selectivity: in the `2.75–4L` annulus, the gate reduces mean release only modestly on captures (`0.113–0.130` to `0.101–0.128`) but nearly eliminates it on the parent’s persistent-error failure (`0.054` to `0.0057`, with 97 fully vetoed release rows). I’m adding those dry-check facts to the provenance note, without treating them as CFD evidence.

Produced exactly one candidate: [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1).

It preserves the proven traveling-bend carrier and steering allocation, adding a continuous course-error veto so steering is not released while redirect error remains large.

Updated:

- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:205)

All required checks pass: guidance difference, Julia policy/schema contract, and editable boundary. Reflection and finite-action probes also pass. No CFD was run. The required checker additionally removed a duplicated parent marker from `README.md`.
